assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and credit cycles gave macroeconomics a formal account of how financial frictions amplify and propagate shocks. The framework became central to financial-crisis analysis and to modern macro-finance and policy models. Its conceptual originality is high and its influence broad.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the credit-cycle mechanism (1997). Gertler is the main extender of the financial-accelerator and quantitative macro-finance line. Gilchrist's contribution is mostly empirical and quantitative, so I leave him out to keep the trio focused on the theoretical core.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of citation, extension and empirical use, including after 2008, so confirmation is ample. Timing is not a constraint.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2022 prize for work on banks and financial crises, and with the Bernanke-Gertler line, could affect how the committee frames novelty.
Whether the committee prefers to credit Gertler or a broader financial-accelerator group is unclear.
My assessment relies on general knowledge and not on independent verification of citations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design turn the choice of information structure into an optimization problem. This is a conceptual advance in the theory of information, mechanism and communication, with uses in market design, regulation and platforms. It sits within the mechanism-design tradition recognised in 2007 and 2020 and is plausibly a distinct new step.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow founded persuasion (2011). Bergemann and Morris generalised it to information design and Bayes correlated equilibrium, with a separate robust-mechanism-design lineage. Gentzkow's broader empirical work on media is a separate contribution. Choosing three of the four is a real judgment call.
assessment.maturity: The core paper dates from about 2011 and the literature is large and still growing. Evidence of real-world impact is thinner than for older candidates.
uncertainties: Which three of the four names are best credited is uncertain.
Empirical or applied impact is less established than the theoretical impact.
The field may be judged slightly early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: These authors built the modern analytical framework for how constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity shape fiscal policy and growth. They combined formal models with systematic empirical tests. The work has shaped political economics and public economics for three decades.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central joint authors of the constitutional and electoral-rules programme. Besley is closely linked through the state-capacity and political-agency work. The attribution is coherent, though the field has several other prominent contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of replication, extension and policy relevance. The recent 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity relates to this area and may affect how its timing is viewed.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2024 prize on institutions could lead the committee to defer political economics.
Besley's inclusion versus other political-economy contributors is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of fairness and inequity aversion, supported by experiments, explain a range of behaviour that standard self-interest models cannot. They reshaped contract theory, public goods and labour-market analysis. The theoretical and experimental parts reinforce each other.
assessment.attribution: The Fehr-Schmidt (1999) model is the clearest formal anchor. Fehr is the dominant experimental and conceptual figure. Falk is a significant contributor, but I propose the two names most tied to the core model. Other contributors, such as Bolton-Ockenfels and Rabin on reciprocity, are not on this credited list.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with a quarter-century of replication. Behavioural and experimental economics have already been recognised (2002, 2017, 2019), which affects marginal novelty but not merit.
uncertainties: The exclusion of Bolton-Ockenfels and Rabin makes the attribution incomplete.
Questions about external validity of lab-based social preferences remain.
Recent behavioural prizes may reduce the priority of the area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data changed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and of neighbourhood effects, and linked the evidence directly to policy design. The substantive findings and the methodological shift are both important. It is influential across labour and public economics.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the central figure. Hendren and Friedman are lead co-authors on key mobility and neighbourhood papers. Katz is credited here but his strongest contributions are elsewhere (for example, the technology-and-inequality literature).
assessment.maturity: Most results are from the last decade. Replication and long-run follow-up are still maturing, although the research has already been widely adopted.
uncertainties: This is a young body of work for a prize, and some findings, such as causal neighbourhood effects, are still being debated.
It is a team-based programme with many collaborators, which makes attribution diffuse.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural demand estimation with differentiated products (BLP) and dynamic industry models made empirical industrial organisation practical. It is used in merger review, regulation and antitrust. It is a clear methodological contribution with a large real-world footprint.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (1995) are the core of the demand-estimation method. Pakes also did substantial work on dynamic games and on the Ericson-Pakes framework. The credited list is long (seven names), so the three-name selection reflects the BLP core.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with thirty years of use and extension in academia and in practice.
uncertainties: Bresnahan's contributions to empirical IO could be argued as equally central.
The dynamic-industry part of the credited work is less closely tied to the BLP trio.
Methodological prizes are weighed against questions about the strength of the identifying assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work connects the theory of adverse selection to measurement and welfare analysis in actual insurance markets. It combines theory, structural methods and quasi-experiments, with direct implications for health policy and market design. The contribution is substantive and consistent in quality.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav are the principal authors of the empirical welfare framework. Salanie is a significant contributor to the econometrics and theory of insurance contracts. The three-way credit is plausible but not tightly bounded.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature, with roughly two decades of work, though the later welfare-measurement results are more recent.
uncertainties: Distinctiveness relative to the earlier information-economics prizes (1996, 2001) is a question.
Whether the committee prefers the empirical or the theoretical credit is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underlies the modern theory and practice of monetary policy analysis. Its lasting use in central banks gives it substantial policy impact. Intellectual importance is high, though the contribution is a long cumulative construction.
assessment.attribution: This is the weakest aspect. The list has eight names, and the work is spread over many hands: Calvo (pricing), Taylor (rules), Woodford and Gali (the canonical framework), and Christiano, Eichenbaum and others (the estimated model). A cap of three names forces exclusions that could be contested.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. Several elements were developed decades ago and are widely confirmed, though their performance in recent inflation episodes has been debated.
uncertainties: The three-laureate limit cannot capture the collective origin of the framework.
Part of the credit overlaps with earlier macroeconomics prizes.
Debate over the framework's performance after the 2021-23 inflation may affect its standing.
